item_6_source_independence_audit.explicit_caveat: Agent count is NOT source independence. 25 agents ran, but agents are consumers of sources, not sources. The counts below are over DOMAINS and ORGANIZATIONS reached, and they further collapse wire-syndicated outlets into a single family because a shared AP or Field Level Media recap republished by six papers is ONE source, not six.
item_6_source_independence_audit.id_note: The 72 includes ids of REJECTED prior-day echo games, deliberately retained as evidence of the rejection.
independence_families: OFFICIAL_LEAGUE (mlb.com incl. baseballsavant, wnba.com incl. team sites, nfl.com incl. team sites)
WIRE_SYNDICATED (AP / Field Level Media republished by local outlets — collapsed to ONE)
each remaining independent outlet counted individually
item_6_source_independence_audit.games_with_two_source_corroboration: 14 of 14 — every game reached at least 5 independent families, minimum observed 5 (SF@CLE, TOR@TB, WSH@TEX)
item_6_source_independence_audit.cross_pass_check: The verification pass and the adversarial refutation pass were run by different agents with different prompts; per game they shared between 1 and 6 domains, meaning each pass also reached domains the other did not.
item_6_source_independence_audit.residual_weakness_stated_plainly: Every game's evidence includes an OFFICIAL_LEAGUE title and an ESPN title. If those two organizations were both wrong in the same direction on the same game, the corroborating independent outlets would in most cases not catch it, because many of them derive their scores from the same league feed. This is a real, unremovable limit of score-provider concentration, not a defect of the fan-out.

item_7_healthcheck_timestamp_diagnosis.observed_delta: The 5d35b23 diff is exactly two lines: checked_utc 06:00:52Z -> 06:01:45Z and built_utc 06:00:52Z -> 06:01:45Z. No substantive field changed.
item_7_healthcheck_timestamp_diagnosis.why_it_matters: Running the read-only verification makes the working tree dirty, so 'uncommitted changes' is not a reliable cleanliness signal immediately after a healthcheck, and the stop-hook fires on every run. It also puts pure-timestamp commits into the release history.
item_7_healthcheck_timestamp_diagnosis.root_cause: The gate artifacts serve two purposes in one file: a versioned report (worth tracking) and a run-liveness stamp (changes every execution by construction). Only the second causes the churn.
options_not_implemented: A: move the timestamp to an untracked sidecar (e.g. data/audit/.last_run.json, gitignored), leaving the tracked report byte-stable when nothing substantive changed
B: write-if-changed — compare the payload excluding the timestamp and skip the write when identical
C: gitignore the two audit artifacts entirely and treat them as local run state
D: accept the churn and keep folding it into a timestamp-only commit, as done for 5d35b23
item_7_healthcheck_timestamp_diagnosis.recommendation_if_authorized: Option B is the smallest change that preserves both purposes: the report still refreshes when a gate result actually moves, and a no-change run leaves the tree clean.
